timeline.message:
Improve toolchain resolution debug logging

* Group logging into a single debug message per (toolchain type, target
  platform) pair
* Use indentation to highlight resolution phases
  1. looking for all toolchains mathing the target platform
  2. looking for all exec platforms matching the said toolchain
* Add a summary message containing all the selected triplets
* Less aggressive printing of exec platform resolution
* Speedup toolchain resolution a bit by stopping search as soon as all
  exec platforms have a toolchain assigned.
timeline.author: Guillaume Maudoux

timeline.body:
* Group logging into a single debug message per (toolchain type, target platform) pair to avoid mixed output lines. This allows to reduce the length of debug lines as repeated information is explicit from the context in the previous lines.
* Use indentation to highlight resolution phases
  1. looking for all toolchains matching the target platform
  2. looking for all exec platforms matching the said toolchain
* Add a summary message containing all the selected triplets
* Less aggressive printing of exec platform resolution
* Speedup toolchain resolution a bit by stopping search as soon as all
  exec platforms have a toolchain assigned.

timeline.body:
The `--toolchain_resolution_debug=regex` flag has two usages:
1. If the regex matches a toolchain type, all attempts to resolve that toolchain type are logged.
   1. This is the most common usage, and we have several help messages telling users to do this.
2. If the regex matches a target that requests a toolchain type, toolchain resolution for that target is logged.
   1. This is what causes the `debugTarget` field on the key to be set.
 
This change is removing the first part: why was it removed?

reply.body:
There are two kinds of debug messages
A. A debug trace of the toolchain resolution for a given toolchain type, and a given target platform. These are multi-line traces.
B. single line target platform selection, based on the first target platform that has all the required toolchain types.

I did it to remove verbosity in case 1. where presumably all the B. messages are less useful and spammy. It seems more useful to get B messages for a given target than for a given toolchain type. B messages are also somewhat redundant, because A. messages already tell which toolchain was selected for which target platform.

So getting all the B messages seems somewhat verbose. Also, the same behavior can be achieved by grepping the toolchain type in the` --toolchain_resolution_debug=.*` output

All in all, because I felt it was better.

I did not realise that such a debug feature was used extensively in tests.
You can see that I had to adapt the tests to use case 2. to recover B. messages that my PR removed in case 1.

Using the flag with a specific toolchain type is unfortunately more verbose, but is definitely something that users expect to be able to do, and we should have a longer planning period before removing that. Please add it back in.

To align everything with the first INFO: line, as in

```
INFO: ToolchainResolution: Performing resolution of @bazel_tools//tools/cpp:toolchain_type for target platform @local_config_platform//:host
      ToolchainResolution:   Rejected toolchain @bazel_tools~cc_configure_extension~local_config_cc//:cc-compiler-armeabi-v7a; mismatching values: armv7, android
      ToolchainResolution:   Toolchain @bazel_tools~cc_configure_extension~local_config_cc//:cc-compiler-k8 is compatible with target plaform, searching for execution platforms:
```

I feel there is no point in having nice indents if you cannot see them, as would be the case with

Then it is as ready as can be I think.
